policy_notes.title: Protect College Sports Act passes the Senate 77–22 (Sep 28, 9:42 PM)
policy_notes.body: S. 4668 (Cruz–Cantwell) codifies the House v. NCAA terms into federal statute: conditional antitrust exemption, preemption of state NIL/transfer laws, five-year eligibility clock, one penalty-free transfer, 5% agent-fee cap via SPARTA. The Booker–Murphy $5M coach-salary-cap amendment failed 51–47. First comprehensive federal bill to clear either chamber. (Senate Commerce Committee; On3 ×3, Sep 28)

policy_notes.title: House resistance and the ACC realignment revolt (Oct 1–2)
policy_notes.body: House leaders draft amendments against Title II's 20-school conference cap and three-year independent penalty ('We won't pass language to blow up the ACC' — Dellenger, On3/Yahoo, Oct 1); Clemson, Florida State, Miami, and North Carolina presidents jointly petition for removal (Schultz, On3, Oct 2). Cozen O'Connor: Senate passage alone imposes no current compliance mandates. Reconciliation must beat the 119th Congress's Jan 3, 2027 expiry.

policy_notes.title: First audited rev-share year: $1.8 billion (Oct 1)
policy_notes.body: College Sports Commission CAPS records: NCAA institutions disbursed ~$1.8B in direct revenue sharing in 2025–26. The 2026–27 cap is $21.58M per school (up from $21.3M after the media-revenue audit); the Senate bill would raise it to $48–49.2M plus a retention fund. NIL Go cleared 7,639 deals worth $227.25M Jul 1–Aug 31 and denied 484 worth $67.08M; 63%+ of submissions come from booster networks. (On3/Byington; On3 CSC report)

policy_notes.title: House v. NCAA judicial track + new eligibility suits
policy_notes.body: Ninth Circuit oral arguments on the Title IX back-damages appeals docketed for Dec 7, 2026 (San Francisco); injunctive revenue-sharing relief remains operative. New suits inside the window: Hall v. NCAA (Sep 29) and Simmons v. NCAA (Oct 2), challenging the exclusion of 2022 enrollees from the five-year eligibility exemptions. (College Sports Litigation Tracker; College Athlete Compensation portal)

policy_notes.title: Collectives: no shutdowns; retention market heats up
policy_notes.body: No prominent collective shutdowns or dissolutions in the window — the sector continues its migration to commercial marketing agencies. NFL All-Pro Chris Jones (Mississippi State alum) pledged direct donor funding to the Bulldogs' collective specifically to retain QB Kamario Taylor amid transfer interest (Kennington Smith III, Front Office Sports, Oct 1).
